faq.question: What does this JSON to code generator produce?
faq.answer: It generates declarations for the selected target: a TypeScript interface, a Python dataclass, a Go struct, or a Rust struct, plus the nested declarations those types reference. The output is inferred from the sample and may need manual changes.

faq.question: Which languages are supported?
faq.answer: TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust. Each target names fields, maps arrays, and handles nullability differently, so review the output for the target you selected.

faq.question: Does it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It generates a useful starting point, not a guaranteed production-ready model. Review naming, optional fields, nullability, serialization behavior, validation, imports, and language-specific conventions before committing the output.

faq.question: Does it generate serialization code?
faq.answer: Partly. Go structs include json struct tags and Rust structs derive Serialize and Deserialize, so those targets carry basic serialization metadata. TypeScript interfaces and Python dataclasses describe the shape only; they add no runtime parsing, validation, or custom converters.

faq.question: How are nested objects handled?
faq.answer: Nested objects are emitted as separate declarations and referenced by the parent type in all four targets. The exact syntax depends on the selected language, and generated names may need to be adjusted when property names are generic or reused.

faq.question: How are JSON arrays handled?
faq.answer: Arrays become Item[] in TypeScript, list[Item] in Python, []Item in Go, and Vec<Item> in Rust. Mixed or inconsistent item shapes produce union types in TypeScript and Python, while Go and Rust fall back to a permissive value type that needs manual modeling.

faq.question: Can one JSON example determine all types correctly?
faq.answer: No. A single sample cannot reveal every optional field, alternative object shape, nullable value, enum, range, or future API variation. Use representative samples and review the generated code against the actual data contract.

faq.question: How are null and optional fields handled?
faq.answer: With "preserve null in types" enabled, a field whose sample value is null becomes null, None, a nullable pointer, or Option depending on the target; with it disabled, such fields become a permissive type such as unknown, Any, interface{}, or serde_json::Value. "Mark fields optional" adds ?, a None default, omitempty, or Option instead. An optional field may be absent, which is different from being present with null.

faq.question: Can I provide multiple JSON samples?
faq.answer: Only if the current interface supports multiple samples or a documented sample-merging mode. Multiple representative samples improve inference for optional fields, mixed arrays, and alternative response shapes.

faq.question: What happens to JSON keys that are not valid identifiers?
faq.answer: The generator may quote, sanitize, rename, or map them according to the selected target. Review the result because changing a generated property name may require a serialization tag or explicit mapping to preserve the original JSON key.

faq.question: Which options are available for each target?
faq.answer: Only the options that apply to the selected target are shown: TypeScript supports export declarations, optional properties, null preservation, format comments, and indentation; Python supports an __all__ export list, optional fields, null preservation, datetime and uuid hints, and indentation; Go supports omitempty tags, null preservation, time.Time hints, and indentation; Rust supports pub export, optional fields, null preservation, and indentation.

faq.question: Does the generated Rust code require external crates?
faq.answer: Yes. Rust output uses serde attributes, and any position whose shape cannot be typed uses serde_json::Value, so add serde and serde_json to your Cargo.toml. TypeScript, Python, and Go output uses only standard language features; the Python output relies on the dataclasses module, and the Go output may import time for date and time fields.

faq.question: Does the generated TypeScript or other code validate runtime JSON?
faq.answer: Usually not. Static models help compilers and editors but do not validate untrusted runtime data. Add a runtime validation layer or generated serializers when the application requires protection against malformed input.

faq.question: Can I use the output directly in an API project?
faq.answer: You can use it as a starting model, but compile or format it, review serialization tags and nullable fields, test it against representative payloads, and adapt it to the framework and library conventions used by your project.

faq.question: Is my JSON uploaded to a server?
faq.answer: This page is designed to parse JSON and generate code in your browser without requiring a server upload. You should still avoid entering credentials, access tokens, private customer data, or confidential production payloads into any browser-based tool.

faq.question: Is this a free JSON to code generator?
faq.answer: Yes. You can paste or open JSON, choose an available target, generate code, and copy or download the result without creating an account.

article.title: How to Generate Code from JSON
article.content:
What Is a JSON to Code Generator?

A JSON to code generator reads a JSON sample and writes declarations for another language. Depending on the target, the output is a TypeScript interface, a Python dataclass, a Go struct, or a Rust struct, plus any nested declarations those types reference.

The generator removes repetitive boilerplate, but it does not know the rules of your application. Treat the result as a starting model that still has to be reviewed, compiled, tested, and adapted to the conventions of the target project.

Common Use Cases

  • API integration: Build initial response models from REST, GraphQL, webhook, or internal service payloads.
  • Frontend development: Create TypeScript types for Vue, React, Angular, or other JavaScript projects.
  • Backend models: Create starting structs or classes for Go, Python, or Rust services.
  • Data contract review: Turn a payload taken from logs or documentation into a readable model before coding against it.

How to Generate Code from JSON

  1. Provide representative input: Paste an object, an array of objects, or open a JSON file. Include optional fields and shape variations that occur in real data.
  2. Select a target: Choose TypeScript, Python, Go, or Rust.
  3. Set the root name: Use a name that describes the model's role, such as UserResponse or Order.
  4. Configure options: Toggle the options shown for that target: export declarations, optional fields, null preservation, format hints, and indentation.
  5. Generate: Read through nested declarations, arrays, and field mappings before trusting them.
  6. Compile and test: Put the output in a real file, run the target compiler or formatter, and feed representative payloads through it.

How JSON Types Map to Code

  • Strings: Become string-like types such as string, str, or String.
  • Numbers: Python, Go, and Rust separate integers and floating-point values as int/float, int/float64, and i64/f64. TypeScript uses number for both.
  • Booleans: Become boolean, bool, or a target-specific equivalent.
  • Objects: Become named declarations: interfaces, classes, or structs.
  • Arrays: Become Item[], list[Item], []Item, or Vec<Item>.
  • Null: Becomes null, None, a pointer, or Option<T> depending on the target and the options you set.

Nested Objects and Naming

Nested JSON objects are emitted as separate named declarations in every supported target. Names are inferred from property names, but properties such as data, items, or value can produce generic or ambiguous names. Rename declarations when the generated names do not describe the domain model clearly.

Property naming also varies by target. Go field names are exported and keep the original JSON key in a struct tag. Rust field names are snake_case and keep the original key in a serde(rename) attribute. Python keeps the key when it can be used as a field name and sanitizes it otherwise, and TypeScript quotes keys that are not valid identifiers. After renaming, confirm that serialization still maps the field back to the original JSON key.

Arrays and Mixed Shapes

An array of objects is straightforward when every item has the same shape. Real API responses often contain variants:

[{"type":"user","name":"Alice"},{"type":"error","code":400,"message":"Bad request"}]

The object variants merge into one model whose fields are marked optional. A union is only produced for mixed primitive values such as numbers and strings, and only in TypeScript and Python; Go and Rust have no union type, so such a position falls back to a permissive value type that you should model by hand.

Optional and Nullable Fields

A field missing from some samples and a field whose value is null are different things. The first means the key may be absent; the second means the key is present with a null value.

  • Optional: TypeScript writes key?, Python adds a None default, Go adds omitempty to the struct tag, and Rust uses Option.
  • Nullable: TypeScript writes T | null, Python writes T | None, Go writes a pointer such as *string, and Rust writes Option<T>.
  • No information: Disabling null preservation turns null-only fields into a permissive type such as unknown, Any, interface{}, or serde_json::Value.

Options That Differ per Target

Each target exposes only the options that make sense for it:

  • TypeScript: export declarations, optional properties, null preservation, format comments, indentation.
  • Python: __all__ export list, optional fields, null preservation, datetime and uuid hints, indentation.
  • Go: optional fields as omitempty, null preservation, time.Time hints, indentation.
  • Rust: pub export, optional fields, null preservation, indentation.

Go exports identifiers through capitalization, so there is no export toggle. Rust has no date type in its standard library, so there is no format hint.

Integer and Floating-Point Numbers

TypeScript has one numeric type, so both 42 and 4.2 become number. Python, Go, and Rust separate them: a sample without a fractional part becomes int, int, or i64, and a sample with one becomes float, float64, or f64. One sample cannot reveal every range, so widen or narrow these types after reviewing the real data contract.

Static Types Are Not Runtime Validation

Generated TypeScript interfaces, Go structs, Python dataclasses, or Rust structs do not automatically validate incoming JSON. External data can be malformed, incomplete, or changed by another service. Add runtime parsing, schema validation, deserialization checks, or generated serializers when the application depends on runtime guarantees.

Use Multiple Samples When Possible

One sample may omit optional fields or fail to show alternative response shapes. Multiple representative samples can improve inference for optional properties, nullable values, mixed arrays, and unions. If the tool accepts only one input document, combine or review representative examples manually before finalizing the model.

Review Generated Code

  • Check field and type names.
  • Verify JSON serialization tags or annotations.
  • Review nullability and optional properties.
  • Check number precision and integer handling.
  • Inspect arrays with mixed item shapes.
  • Run the target compiler or formatter.
  • Test the model with valid and invalid payloads.
  • Keep the generated code synchronized with the actual API contract.

Browser-Based Privacy

This generator is designed to parse JSON and generate code in the browser rather than sending the input to a remote service. That is convenient for API samples and development data, but it is not a secure secret-management system. Avoid entering credentials, tokens, private customer records, or confidential production payloads into any online tool.

faq.question: 这个 JSON 转代码生成器会生成什么？
faq.answer: 它会按所选目标生成声明：TypeScript 接口、Python dataclass、Go 结构体或 Rust 结构体，以及这些类型引用的嵌套声明。输出是基于样本推断的，可能需要手动修改。

faq.question: 支持哪些语言？
faq.answer: 支持 TypeScript、Python、Go 和 Rust。每种语言在字段命名、数组映射和可空处理上都不一样，使用时请针对所选语言检查输出。

faq.question: 生成的是可以直接上生产的代码吗？
faq.answer: 生成的是有用的起点，不是保证可直接用于生产的模型。提交前请检查命名、可选字段、可空性、序列化行为、校验、导入和语言特有的规范。

faq.question: 会生成序列化和反序列化代码吗？
faq.answer: 部分会。Go 结构体带 json 标签，Rust 结构体派生 Serialize 和 Deserialize，因此这两种目标带有基础序列化元数据。TypeScript 接口和 Python dataclass 只描述数据结构，不包含运行时解析、校验或自定义转换器。

faq.question: 嵌套对象怎么处理？
faq.answer: 四种目标都会把嵌套对象生成为独立的命名声明，由父类型引用。具体语法取决于所选语言；当属性名过于通用或重复时，生成的名称可能需要调整。

faq.question: JSON 数组怎么处理？
faq.answer: 数组在 TypeScript 中是 Item[]，Python 中是 list[Item]，Go 中是 []Item，Rust 中是 Vec<Item>。元素形状不一致时，TypeScript 和 Python 会生成联合类型；Go 和 Rust 没有联合类型，会退化为宽松的值类型，需要你手动建模。

faq.question: 一份 JSON 示例就能确定所有类型吗？
faq.answer: 不能。单个样本无法体现所有可选字段、其他对象结构、可空值、枚举、取值范围，也无法预测 API 后续的变化。请使用有代表性的样本，并对照真实数据契约检查生成结果。

faq.question: null 字段和可选字段怎么处理？
faq.answer: 勾选“保留类型中的 null”后，样本值为 null 的字段会按语言变成 null、None、可空指针或 Option；不勾选时，这类字段会变成宽松类型，如 unknown、Any、interface{} 或 serde_json::Value。勾选“字段标记为可选”则会加上 ?、None 默认值、omitempty 或 Option。字段缺失和字段值为 null 是两回事。

faq.question: 可以输入多份 JSON 样本吗？
faq.answer: 取决于当前界面是否支持多样本或提供了明确的样本合并模式。多份有代表性的样本能更好地推断可选字段、混合数组和不同的响应结构。

faq.question: JSON 键不是合法标识符时会怎样？
faq.answer: 生成器会按所选目标进行加引号、清洗、重命名或映射。请检查结果：改名后可能需要序列化标签或显式映射，才能保留原始 JSON 键。

faq.question: 每种语言各有哪些选项？
faq.answer: 界面只显示适用于当前语言的选项：TypeScript 支持导出声明、可选属性、保留 null、格式注释和缩进；Python 支持 __all__ 导出列表、可选字段、保留 null、datetime 与 uuid 提示和缩进；Go 支持 omitempty 标签、保留 null、time.Time 提示和缩进；Rust 支持 pub 导出、可选字段、保留 null 和缩进。

faq.question: 生成的 Rust 代码需要外部依赖吗？
faq.answer: 需要。Rust 输出使用 serde 属性，无法确定类型的字段会用到 serde_json::Value，因此要在 Cargo.toml 中加入 serde 和 serde_json。TypeScript、Python 和 Go 的输出只用到语言自带能力：Python 依赖 dataclasses 模块，Go 在处理日期时间字段时可能导入 time。

faq.question: 生成的 TypeScript 或其他代码能校验运行时 JSON 吗？
faq.answer: 通常不能。静态模型可以帮助编译器和编辑器，但不会校验不可信的运行时数据。如果需要防范异常输入，请额外添加运行时校验层或生成的序列化器。

faq.question: 输出可以直接用在 API 项目里吗？
faq.answer: 可以当作起始模型使用，但要先编译或格式化，检查序列化标签和可空字段，用有代表性的数据做测试，并按项目使用的框架和库规范做调整。

faq.question: 我的 JSON 会上传到服务器吗？
faq.answer: 这个页面在浏览器中解析 JSON 并生成代码，不需要上传到服务器。但仍请避免把凭证、访问令牌、客户隐私数据或生产环境的保密数据粘贴到任何在线工具里。

faq.question: 这是一个免费的 JSON 转代码生成器吗？
faq.answer: 是。你可以粘贴或打开 JSON、选择可用目标、生成代码并复制或下载结果，全程不需要注册账号。

article.title: 如何从 JSON 生成代码
article.content:
什么是 JSON 转代码生成器？

JSON 转代码生成器读取一份 JSON 样本，然后为另一种语言生成声明。根据目标不同，输出可能是 TypeScript 接口、Python dataclass、Go 结构体或 Rust 结构体，以及这些类型引用的嵌套声明。

它帮你省掉重复的样板代码，但并不了解你的应用规则。请把结果当成起始模型，之后仍需检查、编译、测试，并按目标项目的规范做调整。

常见使用场景

  • API 对接：用 REST、GraphQL、webhook 或内部服务的响应样本，生成第一批响应模型。
  • 前端开发：为 Vue、React、Angular 或其他 JavaScript 项目生成 TypeScript 类型。
  • 后端模型：为 Go、Python 或 Rust 服务生成结构体或类的起始版本。
  • 数据契约核对：把日志或文档里的报文转成可读模型，再开始写业务代码。

如何从 JSON 生成代码

  1. 提供有代表性的输入：粘贴对象、对象数组，或打开 JSON 文件。真实数据里存在可选字段或不同结构时，请一并包含。
  2. 选择目标语言：选择 TypeScript、Python、Go 或 Rust。
  3. 设置根类型名称：用能说明模型用途的名称，例如 UserResponse 或 Order。
  4. 配置选项：按当前语言显示的选项调整：导出声明、可选字段、保留 null、格式提示和缩进。
  5. 生成：先看一遍嵌套声明、数组和字段映射，再决定是否采用。
  6. 编译并测试：把输出放进真实文件，运行目标语言的编译器或格式化工具，并用有代表性的数据跑一遍。

JSON 类型如何映射为代码

  • 字符串：变成字符串类型，例如 string、str 或 String。
  • 数字：Python、Go、Rust 会区分整数和浮点数，分别得到 int/float、int/float64、i64/f64。TypeScript 两者都用 number。
  • 布尔值：变成 boolean、bool 或对应语言的等价类型。
  • 对象：变成命名声明：接口、类或结构体。
  • 数组：变成 Item[]、list[Item]、[]Item 或 Vec<Item>。
  • null：根据所选语言和你的选项，变成 null、None、指针或 Option<T>。

嵌套对象与命名

在所有支持的语言中，嵌套 JSON 对象都会生成为独立的命名声明。名称由属性名推导，但 data、items、value 这类属性容易产生通用或含义不清的名称。当生成的名称不能清楚表达领域模型时，请重命名。

字段命名也因语言而异：Go 字段名需要导出，并在结构体标签中保留原始 JSON 键；Rust 字段名用 snake_case，并用 serde(rename) 属性保留原始键；Python 在键可以直接作为字段名时保持不变，否则做清洗；TypeScript 会对非法标识符加引号。重命名后，请确认序列化时字段仍能映射回原始 JSON 键。

数组与混合结构

当数组里每个元素结构都相同时，建模很简单。真实的 API 响应经常出现不同变体：

[{"type":"user","name":"Alice"},{"type":"error","code":400,"message":"Bad request"}]

这些对象变体会合并成一个模型，其中不同的字段被标记为可选。只有在数字、字符串这类基本类型混合时才会生成联合类型，且仅限 TypeScript 和 Python；Go 和 Rust 没有联合类型，遇到这种情况会退化为宽松的值类型，需要你手动建模。

可选字段与可空字段

“部分样本中缺失的字段”和“值为 null 的字段”不是一回事：前者表示这个键可能不存在，后者表示键存在但值为 null。

  • 可选：TypeScript 写成 key?，Python 加 None 默认值，Go 在结构体标签里加 omitempty，Rust 使用 Option。
  • 可空：TypeScript 写成 T | null，Python 写成 T | None，Go 写成 *string 这样的指针，Rust 写成 Option<T>。
  • 信息不足：关闭“保留类型中的 null”后，只有 null 样本的字段会变成宽松类型，如 unknown、Any、interface{} 或 serde_json::Value。

各语言可用的选项

每种语言只显示对它有意义的选项：

  • TypeScript：导出声明、可选属性、保留 null、格式注释、缩进。
  • Python：__all__ 导出列表、可选字段、保留 null、datetime 与 uuid 提示、缩进。
  • Go：用 omitempty 表示可选字段、保留 null、time.Time 提示、缩进。
  • Rust：pub 导出、可选字段、保留 null、缩进。

Go 通过首字母大写来导出标识符，所以没有导出开关；Rust 标准库没有日期类型，所以没有格式提示选项。

整数与浮点数

TypeScript 只有一种数字类型，所以 42 和 4.2 都是 number。Python、Go、Rust 会区分：没有小数部分的样本得到 int、int、i64，有小数部分的样本得到 float、float64、f64。单个样本无法体现全部取值范围，请对照真实数据契约放宽或收紧这些类型。

静态类型不等于运行时校验

生成的 TypeScript 接口、Go 结构体、Python dataclass 或 Rust 结构体都不会自动校验传入的 JSON。外部数据可能格式错误、字段缺失，或者已被其他服务改动。如果应用依赖运行时保证，请额外添加运行时解析、schema 校验、反序列化检查或生成的序列化器。

尽量使用多份样本

单份样本可能漏掉可选字段，也无法体现其他响应结构。多份有代表性的样本能更好地推断可选属性、可空值、混合数组和联合类型。如果工具只接受一份输入，请先人工合并或逐个核对代表性示例，再确定最终模型。

检查生成的代码

  • 检查字段名和类型名。
  • 核对 JSON 序列化标签或注解。
  • 检查可空性和可选属性。
  • 检查数字精度和整数处理。
  • 查看元素结构不一致的数组。
  • 运行目标语言的编译器或格式化工具。
  • 用合法和非法数据测试模型。
  • 让生成的代码与真实 API 契约保持同步。

浏览器端隐私

这个生成器在浏览器中解析 JSON 并生成代码，不需要把数据发送到远程服务。这对 API 样本和开发数据很方便，但它不是密钥管理系统。请不要把凭证、令牌、客户隐私记录或生产环境的保密数据粘贴到任何在线工具里。
